evidence.mission_note: It is a manual, naturally aspirated, low-complexity coupe that genuinely fits the enthusiast-bridge brief and is available in California now. The reported accident and above-market price weigh on the 6-24-month resale goal.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes a 2017 Toyota 86 860 Special Edition with a 6-speed manual, a VIN that decodes consistently, 44,215 claimed miles and a dealer price including all fees. Autotrader's history summary reports an accident or damage event and multiple owners, and nothing in the listing describes the damage or its repair. The photos show a stock-appearing car with an 860 SE appearance. They also show a small irregularity at the front bumper's lower-left grille edge, scuffing on the lower lip, and an object hanging beneath the right rear bumper; each warrants inspection given the accident report. Track history, tune status, clutch condition, tire dates, title brand and service records are all unestablished, partly because the detail page was not captured. The fuel-pump recall item does not apply to a 2017. At $21,784 the asking price is far above the $12,276–$16,577 fair-value range derived from sold BRZ/FR-S comps, though active 86 peers ask $18,500–$23,000.
evidence.next_action: Request the full history report and any accident-repair invoice from California Motor Trade, and confirm in writing that an independent PPI can be done in Norco before any deposit.
